'halo' is ordinary attested Cebuano for mixture in ~25 bodies, including the identical frame ffct-20239 'Unsaon nimo pagbulag ang halo sa asin ug balas?' and ffct-18157/18386/18424/20270/20528/34761, so sagol is a synonym swap on text that was already fine.

Both defects are provable and both repairs are corpus-precedented: 'kasaw' has 0 attestations (this card is the sole 'pagkakasaw' body) while 'pagkasinaw' renders 'shiny' in the parallel physical-properties card, and 'panan-aw' means eyesight in 114 bodies (listed as one sense in ffct-00123) whereas 'panimati' glosses 'your senses' in the sibling process-skill cards dcard-05251/05261/10208/10213; nothing else changed and 'physical property' survives verbatim.

The old 'napulo ka mga kilometro' says ten kilometers against fact_en's 'tens of kilometers' — a number wrong against the English — and 'tinagpulo ka' is the corpus's own rendering of exactly that phrase (ffct-39675 'tinagpulo ka centimeters' for 'tens of centimeters') on standard tinag- distributive morphology; edit is two tokens and 'tephra' is intact.

'maka-ayo' means heal/cure across 51 bodies (bones, wounds, TB), so it mistranslates 'fix' in the card's own carbon-fixation frame, and 'kabit' is the corpus's established verb for that very step in the sibling Calvin-cycle card dcard-07990 ('ang carbon dioxide sa hangin ikabit sa usa ka five-carbon molecule') and dcard-04146; one word changed, 'RuDP' intact.

'magkalibang' means to have diarrhea in all 34 corpus bodies, which is plainly not fact_en's 'tummy rumbles', and 'mosaba ang tiyan' is the corpus's attested rendering of the same English (ffct-04401 'Ngano mosaba ang tiyan…' for 'Why does your stomach growl', ffct-12944 'saba'); only the two occurrences of the one verb changed.

'taob' means high tide in all 55 corpus bodies, so glossing DUCK as 'magtaob' is nonsense against the card's own 'DUCK down', while 'duko' is attested for bending/lowering the head (ffct-01855, 02414, 07622 'magduko', 10095); single-word gloss fix with DUCK and COVER preserved verbatim.

'hanas' means skilled/practised in all 8 corpus bodies, so 'maghanas sa topsoil' cannot render fact_en's 'wash away', and 'makabanlas sa' is attested in the identical erosion frame (ffct-30049 and ffct-32494 on topsoil, ffct-29286 'makabanlas sa tawo ug balay') with 'banlas' already in the card's own terms.

EN asks how a car goes backwards but `balikwas` has no binisaya entry and zero corpus bodies outside this card, while the two-token swap to dictionary-cited `atras [at.ras.] : go back (v.)` (paatras 46 / moatras 9 bodies, and the card's own terms already carry "gear paatras") fixes the sense without touching a single fact.

`makapagligtas` is Tagalog (`ligtas` returns "No results" in Cebuano) and makes the flood "save" a person — an inversion in a safety card — and the one-word fix to `makapatumba` is regular maka-pa- morphology (323 distinct such forms in corpus) on dictionary-listed `tumba : fall, tumble`, whose knock-over sense is the corpus norm (matumba, 100 bodies); emphasis "flash flood" survives verbatim.

`pinakabug-at` says "heaviest" where EN says "richest" (bug-at is weight in all 651 bodies) and `nabuak` says "broken" where EN says "decayed", and the two swaps use `dato : rich` — attested for soil in ffct-32494 "dato nga topsoil" = "rich topsoil" — and `dunot : rotten` (50 bodies), leaving "horizons" intact.
